title: Console API: shadow evals metrics query + aggregated breakdown endpoints
author: Chloe Martin
release_notes: Internal-only Console API endpoints for Shadow Evals metrics queries (timeseries + breakdowns) with RBAC enforcement and cardinality-safe filtering.
description: Adds Console backend endpoints to query Shadow Traffic evaluation metrics and aggregated breakdowns for dashboards + rollout gating. This PR introduces a small query layer over the telemetry rollups produced by ENG-2427 (shadow_eval_* aggregate tables) and exposes them via the Console API with strict RBAC + input validation. Endpoints support: (1) time-series for key KPIs (judge win-rate, format adherence, safety outcomes, latency delta, cost delta, shadow error/drop rates), (2) top-N breakdowns by route/model/region/target, and (3) a lightweight “summary” endpoint used by the dashboard header. All queries are bounded by max time window, max group-by cardinality, and require an explicit filter on account_id + route_id. Notes: this does not expose raw prompts/outputs; only aggregated metrics. Raw event drilldown is intentionally out of scope for beta. Related: PR-48261 emits shadow_eval events; PR-48333 will wire up the UI. Testing: added unit tests for query builder + permission checks; added integration tests against local ClickHouse with fixtures. Rollout: behind feature flag console.shadow_evals.enabled and requires console:shadow_evals:read scope.
commits: console-api/shadow-evals: add metrics query interfaces + DTOs
console-api: implement /shadow-evals/breakdown with topK + bucketed dimensions
rbac: add console:shadow_evals:read scope + route-level permission check
telemetry: add schema mapping for shadow_eval_rollup_v1 tables
tests: integration coverage (clickhouse fixtures) + validation cases
docs: internal endpoint docs + examples for UI team
conversation:
Dylan Brooks (review): Can we ensure these endpoints can’t be used to enumerate routes or models for an account without explicit route filter? Also please call out the max window/topK constraints in the handler, not only in the validator.
Chloe Martin (author): Yep—updated validators to require route_id and added a hard cap in handler (defense in depth). Also added a negative test that omits route_id and expects 400.

Logan Wright (review): Query pattern looks good. One concern: group_by includes "prompt_config_id" in the request type—this will explode cardinality if UI accidentally uses it. We should not allow it in beta.
Chloe Martin (author): Agreed. Removed prompt_config_id from allowed group_by dimensions. We can revisit once ENG-2435 guardrails land end-to-end.

Allison Grant (review): Naming: please keep metric names aligned with shadow_eval.* conventions. Also, can you add an explicit field for “shadow_drop_count” vs “shadow_error_count” so SRE panels match?
Chloe Martin (author): Done—renamed response keys to match observability schema and split drop/error. Added compatibility mapping for older rollups (NULL -> 0).

Jin Woo Park (review): For judge win-rate, are we returning confidence intervals or just point estimate? UI may want error bars.
Chloe Martin (author): Point estimate only for MVP. Added optional fields in response (win_rate_ci_low/high) but only populated when the rollup table includes Wilson interval columns. Left it behind feature flag so UI can safely ignore.

Nadia Rahman (review): Please confirm cost delta uses normalized token pricing (shadow target) not customer billable. We don’t want billing mismatches.
Chloe Martin (author): Uses internal normalized “inference_cost_usd” columns from telemetry rollups; not the billing ledger. Added doc note + renamed field to cost_delta_usd_estimate.

Dylan Brooks (final): Looks good with the route_id requirement + caps. Approving.
notes: Guardrails included: max_time_range_days=30, max_points=2000, max_topk=25, allowed_group_by=[region, shadow_target_id, model_id, route_id], required_filters=[account_id, route_id], and read-only aggregated tables only (no raw payload access).
